intentions.title: Give a new Barkpark adopter a working, deployable Next.js blog in one `create-barkpark-app` scaffold — no manual wiring of client, schemas, or seed data
intentions.evidence: package.json.tmpl wires next/react/@barkpark/{core,nextjs,react,codegen}; barkpark.config.ts.tmpl builds a ready createClient; seeds/seed.ts populates authors/tags/posts against docker-compose in one `pnpm seed` command.

intentions.title: Demonstrate the canonical read-path contract (envelope shape, cache tags, draft mode) as the reference implementation other integrations copy
intentions.evidence: lib/barkpark.ts defines QueryEnvelope/DocEnvelope with count/etag/syncTags, delegates ALL fetching through createBarkparkServer's barkparkFetch so read cache tags match webhook-driven revalidateBarkpark tags, and forces `cache: 'no-store'` under Next.js draftMode().

intentions.title: Prove multi-tenant scoping (`/w/<workspace>/p/<project>/v1/...`) is optional and drops cleanly to the flat `/v1/...` path for single-tenant/local use
intentions.evidence: barkpark.config.ts.tmpl comments explain workspace/project scoping requires a token even for public reads and are left unset by default; seeds/seed.ts computes SCOPE conditionally from WORKSPACE/PROJECT env vars with the same fallback logic.

intentions.title: Model a realistic content graph (post/author/tag with references, slugs, rich text, images) as the template schema for downstream blog/CMS starters
intentions.evidence: schemas/post.ts declares title/slug/excerpt/content(richText)/author(reference)/coverImage(image)/publishedAt/tags(arrayOf reference); seed.ts creates 2 authors, 3 tags, 7 posts (6 published + 1 intentionally-draft) exercising every field type and the publish mutation.

intentions.title: Pre-stage the ADR-003 typed-query/codegen migration path without blocking today's per-type query API
intentions.evidence: lib/queries.ts holds GROQ-like query strings explicitly marked informational ('ready for the codegen + typed-query migration, ADR-003 Phase 8') while pages actually call typed helpers in lib/barkpark.ts; package.json.tmpl ships `codegen: barkpark generate` script already wired for that future.

intentions.title: Ensure slug lookups never return the wrong document even if server-side filtering is imprecise
intentions.evidence: getDocBySlug in lib/barkpark.ts filters server-side via makeFilterExpression('slug.current','eq',slug) then re-validates client-side with docs.find(...) as an explicit safety net, per its inline comment.
